hints.title: Two Button Keystrokes
hints.text: Button 1 always appends character 'a'. Button 2 changes the last character cyclically to the next character in the alphabet.

hints.title: Incremental Character Generation
hints.text: For each character in target, first append 'a' and record the screen string. Then cycle the last character from 'b' up to target[i].

hints.title: Sequential Step Recording
hints.text: Append the modified string to the result list at every single button press until reaching the full target string.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def stringSequence(self, target: str) -> list[str]:
        ans = []
        curr = ""
        for ch in target:
            # Button 1 appends 'a'
            curr += 'a'
            ans.append(curr)
            # Button 2 cycles up to ch
            for code in range(ord('b'), ord(ch) + 1):
                curr = curr[:-1] + chr(code)
                ans.append(curr)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: At most 26 string operations per character in target.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Direct generation is linear and optimal.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(|target| * 26) memory to store the resulting list of strings.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean string state manipulation following exact keyboard operation rules.
